solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dancing adepts incorporating half of dance leap on stage (9, three words)

indicators.note: letters that are dancing are moving about into a new order
to incorporate is to take something into the body of another
only one of the two equal parts of the word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the dance is the cha-cha, and half of it is its first three letters

explanation.surface: Skilled performers dance with a fragment of a dance routine woven in.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance is the cha-cha, a Latin ballroom dance whose name is the same word said twice, so its half is easy to take.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas de chat, French for cat's step, is a ballet jump in which the legs are drawn up like a leaping cat.

clue.text: Folded what's delicate in hamper

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other, as a thing sits in a basket

blocks.note: light, as in a light touch, is delicate
a ped is a dialect word for a hamper or pannier basket

explanation.surface: Someone packs something fragile, wrapped up, into a picnic hamper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like the verb to hinder, but it is the basket, in a dialect word Chambers lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Plighted is an old, Spenserian word for pleated, so folded is a direct archaic synonym.

clue.text: Sardinia's capital – large part of that's limestone

indicators.note: a capital is a word's opening letter, the one written large
taking only most of a word means dropping its tail end

blocks.note: the first letter of Sardinia
that is Sardinia's capital city, Cagliari, cut short by its last two letters

explanation.surface: A geology note claims most of Sardinia's capital city is built of limestone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' does double duty: the capital letter of Sardinia, and 'that' pointing back to the capital city, Cagliari.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaglia is an Italian term for a fine-grained, often reddish limestone of the Alps and Apennines.

clue.text: US plant needing help raised round cemetery near Washington

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it upward, from bottom to top
one piece goes all the way around the other

blocks.note: aid is help
Arlington National Cemetery lies across the Potomac from Washington DC

explanation.surface: An American plant needs a helping hand to grow around a famous military burial ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The raised word is split in two, its first letter before the cemetery and its last two after.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlingtonia is the cobra lily, a carnivorous pitcher plant native to California and Oregon.

clue.text: What's this, one containing soft herrings?

indicators.note: the first word holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: what you are reading right now is the clue
p, piano, is the musical mark for soft
a means one

explanation.surface: A puzzled diner asks what this soft, single fish is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's this' points at the clue itself: CLUE holds P, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Clupea is the scientific genus name of the herrings, including the Atlantic herring.

clue.text: Spring festival's attended by millions in all-embracing philosophy

blocks.note: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours, plus the 's
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A spring festival drawing millions is described as an inclusive way of thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Holi is the Hindu festival of colours celebrated in spring. 'Attended by' simply means followed by.
explanation.definitionFit: Holism is the philosophy that wholes are more than the sum of their parts, so it takes everything in at once.

clue.text: Energy lost in trek replaced with red cheese sandwiches (bulky)

indicators.note: a letter that is lost drops out of the word
the letters are put back in different places

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reorganises a hike, swapping in red cheese for the sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: TREK loses its E to leave TRK, which is mixed with RED CHEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-deckers are sandwiches built of three slices of bread, notably bulky ones; the word also means hefty three-volume novels.

clue.text: Flower I held in palm

indicators.note: something held in a hand is enclosed by it

blocks.note: taken as written
vola is the anatomical name for the palm of the hand or sole of the foot

explanation.surface: Someone holds a flower in their open hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm' looks like the tree, but it is the hand's palm, VOLA in anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A viola is a garden flower of the violet family, close kin to the pansy.

clue.text: Car panel, French article fitted in Packard?

indicators.note: a part fitted in something is installed inside it

blocks.note: le is a French word for the
Vance Packard was the American author of The Hidden Persuaders; the question mark flags the leap to his first name

explanation.surface: A body panel for a car, imported from France, is fitted to a Packard automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: Packard was also an American car make, which is why the car reading feels natural; here it is the writer Vance Packard.
explanation.definitionFit: A valence, usually spelt valance, is a panel on a car body below the bumpers, named after the hanging drapery.

clue.text: Succumb to sleepiness, an inevitable part of table talk

indicators.note: the letters are found as a piece inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Dozing off is an unavoidable feature of dinner-table conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleepiness here is not drowsiness but the soft, overripe state of a pear, called sleepy.
explanation.definitionFit: To blet is for fruit to go soft and overripe, and a sleepy pear is one in that state.

clue.text: Ancient author describing portion of holy scripture

blocks.note: first meaning: the Roman poet of the first century AD, author of the Pharsalia
second meaning: an adjective for things relating to the gospel of St Luke

explanation.surface: A classical writer depicts a section of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' looks like a container signal but is just the start of the second definition: an adjective describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucan names the Latin epic poet, and also serves as the adjective for the evangelist Luke and his gospel.

clue.text: You aim for Mecca, every last one – in this?

definitions.text: You aim for Mecca, every last one – in this?

indicators.note: the final letter of each word in turn is taken

blocks.note: the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A question: is this the journey on which a pilgrim heads to Mecca?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the umra is a pilgrimage whose goal is Mecca.
explanation.definitionFit: The umra is the lesser Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca, which can be made at any time of year.

clue.text: Love child I enveloped in all liquid of post-partum discharge

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so these letters take a new order
a thing enveloped in another is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
ch is the abbreviation for child
taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A love child is wrapped up in fluid after birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' reads as a noun beside discharge, but it works on 'all' just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lochia is the discharge from the womb after childbirth, and lochial is its adjective.

clue.text: Oriental porcelain damage has cracked classical pair

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: to mar is to damage
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Two antique Eastern vases have been chipped and cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical' points to Roman numerals, so the pair is II.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is Japanese porcelain, richly coloured in blue, red and gold, named after the port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Director's leading part for comic

indicators.note: the leading letter of a word is the one at its front

blocks.note: the first letter of director
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A film director's starring role is offered to a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading part' reads as a starring role, but 'leading' belongs with Director's, selecting its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Drole, from the French drôle, is an adjective meaning amusing or funny, a direct synonym of comic.

clue.text: Special crumpet, showing beginning of new florescence

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for special
a pikelet is a thin crumpet or small pancake

explanation.surface: A special crumpet appears at the dawn of a new flowering.
explanation.walkthrough: A pikelet is a flat British or antipodean crumpet, eaten toasted with butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spikelet is a small spike of florets in a grass flower head, the start of its flowering.

clue.text: Compound, robust, I had installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside a larger thing

blocks.note: hale means healthy and robust
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A chemist says a sturdy compound was fitted at their own works.
explanation.definitionFit: A halide is a chemical compound of a halogen with another element, like sodium chloride.

clue.text: Handled containers of stone as sent for repackaging

indicators.note: packed again, the letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Stone jars with handles are being shipped off for new packing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stean is a stone or earthenware jar, often with two handles, used for storing food.

clue.text: Loss City's suffering, denoting a certain physical collapse

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, knocked out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A defeated football club's slump is described as a collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loss City' sounds like a beaten football team, and the collapse is not a team's but the heart's.
explanation.definitionFit: Systole is the contraction of the heart that pumps blood out, and systolic is its adjective.

clue.text: Slim and lively for US hootenanny

blocks.note: slim means thin
gamy can mean spirited or plucky

explanation.surface: A slender, energetic person is just the thing for a folk music night in America.
explanation.walkthrough: A hootenanny is usually a folk-singing party, but in US slang it is also a gadget whose name you've forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a hootenanny is a whatsit or gizmo, the same as a thingamy.

clue.text: Explosive carbamide containing potassium, a brilliant invention

indicators.note: one word holds another within it

blocks.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
carbamide is the chemical name of urea
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A chemist mixes an explosive compound with potassium and hails it as genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Heureka, a variant of eureka, is the cry of discovery and, as a noun, a lucky or brilliant find.

clue.text: Guy in tutu's distributed snuff? (7, two words)

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other before the mixing
letters distributed are scattered into new places

blocks.note: bo is American slang for a fellow or pal
taken as written, with the s

explanation.surface: A man in a ballet skirt hands out snuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snuff' looks like a noun, tobacco being handed round, but it is the verb, with the question mark admitting the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To stub out a cigarette is to press it out against something, extinguishing it as you would snuff a candle.

clue.text: Gets together before food, unravelling secret

indicators.note: something unravelling comes apart and loses its order

blocks.note: ac, ante cibum, is the prescription abbreviation for before meals
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Friends meet up before dinner and a secret comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is Latin ante cibum, written on prescriptions for medicine to take before meals.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by things gathering and adhering together, so it collects.

clue.text: Manger to come upon, containing last of fodder

indicators.note: the first word holds the single letter within it
the final letter of the next word is the one taken

blocks.note: to catch someone at something is to come upon them
the last letter of fodder

explanation.surface: A farmhand finds a feeding trough with the last of the animal feed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cratch is a rack or crib from which animals eat hay, the same thing as a manger.

clue.text: Mix new chocolate? A lot we ——, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could also be arranged another way

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are spent on the first half of the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A chocolatier asks whether we should stir up a big batch of new chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash stands for the answer: NEW CHOCOLATE rearranged reads A LOT WE plus the six letters that fill the blank.
explanation.definitionFit: To conche is to knead and mix liquid chocolate for hours in a machine to make it smooth.

clue.text: It's red at sea (or sort of red, bow to stern and vice versa)

indicators.text: bow to stern and vice versa
indicators.note: the front letter goes to the back and the back letter to the front, swapping places

blocks.note: rusted metal has a reddish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A sailor explains that the ship's flag is red, or rust-coloured, from front to back.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first and last letters of RUSTED. The Red Duster is sailors' slang for the Red Ensign, the British merchant navy flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The British merchant flag at sea is nicknamed the Red Duster, so the duster is the red thing flying there.

clue.text: Sensation over source of poodle pedigree

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: a stir is a sensation or commotion
the first letter of poodle

explanation.surface: A dog-show sensation is caused by a poodle's family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' means the first piece is placed above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirp is a line of descent or family stock, the same as lineage or pedigree.

clue.text: Mysterious chapters ingested, lout reformed

indicators.note: something ingested is taken inside the body
something reformed is made into a new form

blocks.note: c is the abbreviation for chapter, doubled for the plural
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A thug has swallowed some chapters of a strange book and turned over a new leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult means hidden, secret or beyond ordinary understanding, which is what is mysterious.

clue.text: Receive education in local school in Killarney

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the place name that follows

blocks.note: the letters sit inside the Irish town name

explanation.surface: A pupil is taught at a village school in Killarney, a town in County Kerry, Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In local' marks a dialect word: larn is how learn is said in country speech, used both for learning and for schooling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Larn is a dialect form of learn, meaning both to be taught and, as a verb, to teach or school someone.

clue.text: Bonnes bouches maybe for being served in French city, not English

indicators.note: food served in a place is put inside it
not means the following letter is left out

blocks.note: for and to can both mean towards or as regards
Orléans is a city on the Loire
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Delicacies served in a French city, but not English ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word, but it supplies two letters itself; for and to swap in phrases like the key for the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Ortolans are small buntings eaten whole in France as a prized delicacy, so they are tasty morsels, bonnes bouches.

clue.text: E.g. Leipziger half set firmly in his ways?

indicators.note: half of a word means only one of its two halves survives

blocks.note: a person who has ossified has become rigid in their habits

explanation.surface: A man from Leipzig is half stuck in his old habits.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossi is German slang for someone from the former East Germany, where Leipzig lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Leipzig is in the old East Germany, so a native of it is an example of an Ossi, an Easterner.

clue.text: It may reveal catch of grilse I net

definitions.text: It may reveal catch of grilse I net

indicators.note: the letters are shown lying within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: An angler says that what they land will show whether they have grilse, which are young salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a seine is a net, and drawing it up reveals the fish caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A seine is a large fishing net that hangs vertically and is drawn round to enclose a catch.

clue.text: Boss rival disheartened? He was free but lowly

indicators.note: losing its heart leaves only the outer letters of the word

blocks.note: a CEO, chief executive officer, is the boss
the outer letters of rival

explanation.surface: A boss's competitor is discouraged; he once had freedom but little status.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceorl was a freeman of the lowest rank in Anglo-Saxon England, free but not noble.

clue.text: Skirl I reck, upset, penetrating silence

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and out of order
to penetrate is to go inside

blocks.note: sh is the call for silence
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scot cares that a bagpipe's wail is upset by being shushed.
explanation.walkthrough: A skirl is the shrill sound of bagpipes, and reck is an old word for to care.
explanation.definitionFit: Skriech is Scots for a screech, and a skirl is likewise a shrill cry or scream.

clue.text: Head of state's partner, so she's un-Boris in a way

indicators.note: in a way means the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: the word so is the part of the rearrangement already accounted for
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A president's wife is described as quite unlike Boris Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'so she's un-Boris' as SO plus the answer forming an anagram of UNBORIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Carla Bruni, singer and model, married Nicolas Sarkozy while he was President of France.

clue.text: I act uneasily about robbery, being sceptical

indicators.note: acting uneasily means behaving out of the normal order
about means around the outside of something

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A nervous robber says they feel guilty about a theft and doubt everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheistic means denying God's existence, a sceptical stance towards religious belief.
